judgment_calls_for_kilian.question: BKNG valuation legs: keep P/E 60% + FCF yield 40%, or move to P/E only?
judgment_calls_for_kilian.context: BKNG is valued on two legs: NTM P/E at 13.3x on our adjusted EPS (60%) and an 8% FCF yield on our FCF per share (40%). The 60/40 split came from the October base round's supervisor ('a 60/40 blend gives ~$191'), before two later decisions: the 2026-11-16 peer method (P/E on our EPS for profitable names) and the 2026-11-17 FCF leg policy, which adds a 40% FCF leg only for IT and three internet names because the walk-forward test found FCF earns weight there (~0.5) but little elsewhere (~0.1). BKNG is Consumer Discretionary, so under those rules its FCF leg has no tested basis. The FCF leg values BKNG higher ($194.58 vs $171.88) because its FCF runs ~20-22% above adjusted net income: non-cash costs (SBC, provisions) plus customer prepayments (deferred merchant bookings) that grow with bookings; the set now builds that from bookings growth (FCF / NI 1.22 falling to 1.20 by FY2029, 'FCF conversion' row). Option figures re-sized 2026-11-19 (gate round 3) on the current set, research target (12m) 170.58 with the decided option booked; each option's effect is now measured from that booked set.

options.label: P/E only (recommended)
options.reasoning: Matches the 2026-11-16 peer method and the 2026-11-17 leg study: outside tech the FCF leg added little out of sample, and part of BKNG's FCF is customer prepayments (deferred merchant bookings) that shrink as bookings growth slows.

options.label: P/E 90% + FCF 10%
options.reasoning: Takes the study's walk-forward FCF weight outside tech (~0.1) literally, keeping a small FCF check on a business whose cash conversion is real and durable while bookings grow.

options.label: Keep 60/40
options.reasoning: BKNG converts earnings to cash unusually well (FCF 1.22x adjusted NI in FY2025, 1.24x in FY2024; releases) and holders price it on FCF; the base round chose this split with the forecasters, and nothing in the print argues against it.

judgment_calls_for_kilian.why: The split predates the rules Kilian set on 11-16 and 11-17, and the study gives the FCF leg no edge outside tech.

judgment_calls_resolved.question: BKNG dividends FY2027-29: how should the dividend grow?
judgment_calls_resolved.context: Cash returned is FCF either way; the dividend only decides how much of it goes to buybacks, so the share count moves slightly. The board has declared $0.42 a quarter and has no stated growth policy. Its two raises so far (2025 +9.7%, 2026 +9.4%) were about half of EPS growth (0.44 and 0.63), and the set extends that 0.54 ratio. The gate flags this as trend-only. All options move the research target (12m) by under 0.2%.

options.label: Half of EPS growth (booked)
options.reasoning: DPS grows 0.54 x EPS growth, the average of the board's two raises: $1.80 / $1.93 / $2.06.

options.label: Held at $0.42 a quarter
options.reasoning: Dividend held at the declared $0.42 a quarter ($1.68) through FY2029; the difference goes to buybacks; only the declared dividend, no assumed raise.

options.label: Grows with EPS
options.reasoning: Dividend grows with EPS one for one (payout held): less goes to buybacks; the payout ratio stays at today's level.

judgment_calls_resolved.why: It uses only what the board has declared and needs no fitted ratio; the value effect is +0.1%.

judgment_calls_resolved.question: BKNG room nights FY2027-29: how fast does Booking keep gaining share over the travel market?
judgment_calls_resolved.context: Room nights are now built as travel market growth plus Booking's share gain. The market part is sourced: WTTC forecasts travel and tourism growth of +3.6% a year to 2036 (May 2026) and measured +4.1% for 2025. Booking's room nights grew +7.95% in FY2025 (a +3.85pt gain over WTTC) and about +5.4% in FY2026 (+2.16pt; Q4 at the guide). No forecaster gives Booking's share gain for 2027-29, so the gain is a call. The gate flags my booked path (the gain keeps narrowing at its 2025-26 rate) as trend-only, and the Q4 Middle East disruption behind part of the 2026 narrowing is one-off. A related outside figure: Phocuswright (July 2026) has OTA share of US travel rising from 20% to 21% by 2028, US only. WTTC measures travel GDP, not room-night volume.

options.label: Gain keeps narrowing (booked)
options.reasoning: The gain fell from +3.85pt to +2.16pt in a year as the base grew; letting it narrow at that rate gives +4.8% / +4.3% / +4.0%. Moderately conservative, but it extends one past step.

options.label: Gain held at +2.2pt
options.reasoning: Share gain held at FY2026's +2.16pt over WTTC's +3.6%: room nights +5.76% a year FY2027-29: the 2026 narrowing partly reflects the one-off Middle East disruption, and OTAs still gain share in the US (Phocuswright 2026). Gives +5.8% a year.

options.label: No share gain
options.reasoning: No share gain: room nights grow with the WTTC market, +3.6% a year FY2027-29: the most conservative read, Booking only keeps pace with travel as online penetration matures.

judgment_calls_resolved.why: It sits between the two sourced ends and fits a moderately conservative base case; the 2026 slowdown was broad (Q2 and Q3 also slowed), not only the Middle East.
